rationale: The agent appeared to authenticate by looking up the user via name and ZIP and retrieving user details, and accessed an order. However, it proceeded to modify two items in the pending order using a gift card payment method without clear evidence of prior user confirmation. Per the scenario, if asked to confirm payment, the user would have switched to PayPal and only modified the backpack, which did not occur—suggesting confirmation was not obtained. After modifying items, the agent then stated that shipping address changes are not allowed post-modification and transferred to a human. This left the primary request (changing the shipping address to the user's default) unfulfilled. Additionally, the claim about address-change restrictions is not supported by any tool output shown. Policy requires confirmation before any order-changing write and completing the user’s request or appropriate handoff. While handoff is allowed when the request cannot be handled, the agent should have prioritized or confirmed the address change before making item modifications that allegedly prevented it. Therefore, the agent did not complete the user’s request in line with policy and likely performed writes without confirmation.
